title: Halfway to the Wall Forever: Limits Explained Simply | Class 11 Maths
description:
Stand 8 metres from a wall and walk half the way, then half of what is left, again and again. After 20 moves the gap is thinner than a hair, but there is always half left. In this animated lesson for Class 11 Maths (NCERT Chapter 12, Limits and Derivatives) we turn that walk into the idea of a limit.

You will watch x creep up on 2 from the left and from the right while a live table fills and a point slides along a graph with a hole in it. We see why h(x) = (x^2 - 4)/(x - 2) has no value at 2 but still has the limit 4, compare the value at a point with the limit at a point, and meet the left hand and right hand limits with the greatest integer function. Then a worked example, the exam trap about checking only one side, an original JEE Main pattern question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

Follows the NCERT book. Useful for CBSE, ICSE (ISC), Karnataka PUC and other state boards, and JEE.

In this video:
0:00 Halfway to the wall, forever
0:30 What a limit means
0:58 Live: creep up on x = 2 from both sides
1:43 Why the limit is 4
2:18 Value at a point vs limit at a point
2:50 Left hand and right hand limits
3:35 Worked example
4:20 Exam trap: checking only one side
4:43 Where it is asked
4:53 Practice question (JEE Main pattern)
5:23 Recap and three questions to answer

Next episode (Ep 81): Algebra of Limits. A big limit full of sums, products and fractions: can you break it into small ones?
